name: Pre-Mortem Analysis
use_case: A prospective-hindsight exercise in which the team imagines that a plan has already failed badly and then writes the story of how that happened, surfacing risks that optimism and group consensus normally suppress. Best used just before committing to a launch, a migration or a large investment, when the plan looks agreed and nobody is voicing doubts, which is exactly the moment when unspoken concerns are most expensive to leave unspoken.
strengths: licenses dissent by making failure the premise instead of an accusation
prospective hindsight measurably improves how specific risk statements are
catches risks that a confident, cohesive group would otherwise suppress
cheap relative to the size of decision it protects
weaknesses: needs genuine psychological safety or it produces only polite risks
generates a risk list with no inherent prioritization or ownership
can degenerate into pessimism theatre if run too late to change anything
loses its effect when repeated on the same plan with the same people
